messages.body_plain:
Hello, I've been reading database <http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/dplyr/vignettes/databases.html> vignette and got excited by the compute() command for use of Shiny reactive filtering on a large database.

But this got me thinking.  For a large database, say 1-2 TB, and shiny app on a very large machine, do you think it is better practice to:

A.  As user filters, use compute(), and reactively update results with the resulting remote tbl.

B.  Don't use a database.  Break the database into a directory of .rds files based on the first filter levels.  Each .rds fits into memory easily, so for the first filter, readRDS( the appropriate .rds), and reactively filter the .rds from there as user applies additional filters.  Same as before - reactively update results with the local tbl.

Breaking into .rds files could be extended further to keep each file small enough for memory.  It seems like the advice would be to use strategy B until the data can't fit onto disk.

Seems strange to me not to use a database with this much data, so I wanted to know what the recommended or best practice is.  Thanks.

I've been experimenting with dplyr, reading about NSE, and googling, but don't understand why this simple example doesn't work. Simple example:

library(dplyr)
d <- data.frame(x=c(1,1,2,2), y=1:4)  # sample data

f_dplyr <- function(d, FUN, ...) {
group_by(d, x) %>% summarise(y=FUN(y, ...))
}

f_aggregate <- function(d, FUN, ...) {
aggregate(y~x, d, FUN=FUN, ...)
}

print(f_aggregate(d, weighted.mean, c(1,2)))  # this works

print(f_dplyr(d, weighted.mean, c(1,2)))  # this does not--no output

Thanks,
Ben

>> 3    1     1  6      4    write     0

It is not present as a column name. You cannot just pull out some rows
and put them in columns. It's all or nothing.

>
> ***Here's a simple example with no ply functions.  Essentially I'm trying to reconstruct the original df from the melted data:
>     msmall <- matrix(101:106, nrow=2)

df <- data.frame(x=rnorm(3000000), y=sample(0:5000, 3000000, replace=T))

What could be the reason? Do you see the same?

Thanks!
Mike

I had written a suggestion using reshape2, when Hadley sent his similar approach with tidyr (another cool package! I hadn't used it yet).

To add some value, I put our 3 suggestions up against each other with microbenchmark. (I wanted to include Hadley's with tidyr but get an Error: index out of bounds when running his code).

The upshot: Robbie/ Hadley outperform on this small example dataset. For a similar structure with 3 million rows, the reshape strategy seems much faster. See below for the details.

- Jaime

library(dplyr)
## robbie
Robbie <- function(df) {

    df %>% group_by( group ) %>%
        summarise(
            t1t = sum( ifelse( c1 == "t", v1, 0 ) )
            , t1u = sum( ifelse( c1 == "u", v1, 0 ) )
            , t1v = sum( ifelse( c1 == "v", v1, 0 ) )
            )
}

## hadley 1
Hadley1 <- function(df) {
    df %>%
        group_by(group) %>%
            summarise(

                t1t = sum(v1[c1 == "t"]),
                t1u = sum(v1[c1 == "u"]),
                t1v = sum(v1[c1 == "v"]))
}

## hadley 2
library("tidyr")
Hadley2<- function(df) {
    ## require tidyr

    df %>%
        group_by(group, c1) %>%
            summarise(t1 = sum(v1)) %>%
                spread(c1, t1)
}

## mine
library(reshape2)
Jaime <- function(df) {
    ## require reshape2

    df %>% group_by(group, c1) %>%

        summarize(condsum = sum(v1)) %>%
            melt(value.name <http://value.name>='condsum', id.vars=c('group', 'c1')) %>%
                dcast(group ~ c1, value.var='condsum')
}

## let's do some benchmarking
library(microbenchmark)

set.seed( 1 )
N <- 30
df <- data.frame( group=sample( letters[1:4], N, replace=T)
                 , c1=sample( letters[20:22], N, replace=T)
                 , v1 = rbinom( N, 1, .5 )
                 , c2=sample( letters[20:22], N, replace=T)
                 , v2 = rbinom( N, 1, .5 )
                 )
## tidyr solution throws error so don't include :(
##> Hadley2(df)
##Error: index out of bounds

microbenchmark(
    Robbie(df),
    Hadley1(df),
